thread:
IncidentBot: PAGER — sev2: canary anomaly for model redwood-3b-q8 in us-west2. Canary cohort 7 showing increased failure rate and latency. Link: <https://logs.redwood/canary/2961234567>
Alicia: I'm on pager. Can anyone confirm customer impact?
Sam: Seeing spike in canary error-rate 06:42->06:48 UTC. Errors are 5xx model-timeout and some invalid-json responses.
Marco: Confirmed. Dashboard: canary error_rate up 4.2x vs baseline, p95 latency from 350ms -> 1.9s.
Priya: Which rollout batch is this? Canary 7 was pinned to redwood-3b-q8.v2.1 last night.
Jonah: Yup v2.1. Baseline is v2.0. Canary started at 01:00 UTC. No config changes since.
Alicia: Opening quick bridge: zoom.me/123456 (only if needed). For now let's collect logs and hypotheses here.
Rachel: Sharing raw logs snippet: 
```
[06:45:12] request_id=abc123 shard=cache-2 decode_error: KV cache miss -> fallback decode path
[06:45:12] request_id=abc123 model_latency=1870ms backend_timeout
[06:45:13] request_id=def456 json_parse_error: unexpected token at pos 102
```
Sam: Looks like prefix/KV cache miss causing fallback Q8 decode path + timeouts. Pattern across multiple requests.
Marco: I see increased memory pressure on the q8 decoder worker pods around that time. Node kube_eviction events at 06:44.
Priya: Are there any autoscaler spikes/rollbacks? No recent deploys to infra. Autoscaler show spike in pod scale-up but throttled by quota.
Alicia: Hypothesis 1: new quantized v2.1 increases memory per-worker -> cache miss + OOM-triggered evictions -> increased latency/errors.
Jonah: Hypothesis 2: workload changed (longer sequences) causing KV cache growth and causing cache eviction cascades. Need sequence length distribution for canary cohort.
Rachel: Pulling seq len hist from logs: 90th pct seq_len up from 128 -> 512 in canary window. Attaching link: <https://metrics.redwood/seqlen/2961234567>
OpsLead: Customer impact check: no major tenants impacted yet — only traffic routed to canary cohort (5% of traffic). But two paying customers reported degraded latencies in support tickets.
Alicia: OK we need live mitigation. Options: 1) Pin canary to baseline v2.0, 2) Roll back canary, 3) Fix autoscaler/quota quickly, 4) Reduce canary traffic to 1%. Thoughts?
Sam: Immediate: reduce canary traffic to 1% and scale down parallelism for q8 workers. That buys time.
Marco: I can reduce canary weight in routing config: `curl -XPOST https://controlplane/api/rollouts/296 -d '{"weight":1}'` — doing it now.
Marco: Done. Canary weight moved to 1% at 06:50 UTC.
Jonah: I'm increasing `MODEL_MAX_BATCH` to reduce per-request memory spikes? That's risky — could increase latency. Prefer scale or pin.
Priya: Quota request to infra for extra nodes is in progress, but ETA ~20m. Not immediate.
Rachel: Continued log sampling after weight reduction shows error-rate dropping from 4.2x -> 1.3x over 3 minutes. p95 latency trending down.
Alicia: Good. While we stabilize, we should decide: pin or rollback. We need pinned-version checks (are there any known regressions pinned to v2.1). Sam, pls run `modelctl checks --version v2.1 --pin-compat` and paste results.
Sam: Running now...
Sam: Results: `modelctl checks v2.1` -> memory footprint +12% vs v2.0 on q8 path. Quant decode path marked experimental for long sequences. No failing unit tests.
Alicia: That aligns with memory hypothesis. OpsLead: are we comfortable letting v2.1 continue at 1% with autoscaler fixes and longer QA, or roll back to v2.0 for canary?
OpsLead: Given customer reports and mem footprint, recommend pin to v2.0 for canary until we have mitigations. We should also open a rollback if needed.
Marco: I can pin canary route to v2.0 immediately: `controlplane rollout pin --route canary-7 --version v2.0`. Will anyone be impacted by transient routing change?
Jonah: Safe to pin. But confirm model artifact v2.0 still present on all regions; otherwise will trigger fetch delays.
Rachel: Artifact check: v2.0 available in us-west2 and us-east1. Good.
Marco: Pin executed at 06:57 UTC. Canary now serving v2.0.
Sam: Post-pin metrics: error-rate back to baseline 06:59, p95 latency trending normal. No more json parse errors.
Alicia: Great. Triage checklist: - open RCA ticket, - collect full timeline & logs, - reproduce memory spike in staging with longer sequences, - add a guard in rollout pipeline to block v2.x q8 variants for sequences >256 until tested.
Priya: I'll create infra ticket for autoscaler quota and temp node bump for canary.
Rachel: I'll export canary diffs: per-prompt quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxy) and hallucination-rate. Early diff shows hallucination rate (false facts) +1.8x on v2.1 for long sequences. Link: <https://evals.redwood/canary-diffs/2961234567>
Jonah: Note for the RCA: add check 'quant path long-seq tested' to model onboarding checklist.
OpsLead: Decision summary (07:05 UTC): Reduced canary to 1%, pinned canary back to v2.0, no broader rollback required. Impact: limited to 5% cohort, two customer complaints. Next actions: reproduce, add check, quota request.
Alicia: Assigning owners: RCA doc owner = Rachel, Repro owner = Jonah, Autoscale/infra = Priya, Model team follow-up = Sam + Marco.
Marco: I'll also add a temporary monitor to alert if seq_len_90 > 256 for any canary cohort.
Rachel: Uploading logs archive and timeline: <https://artifacts.redwood/canary-2961234567/logs.tar.gz>
Sam: Add to RCA: details of `modelctl` check outputs + memory profiles at varying batch sizes.
Alicia: Thanks everyone. We'll regroup in the RCA doc. If anything regresses re-open this thread or ping oncall. IncidentBot: updating incident status -> mitigated (07:12 UTC).
IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring.
OpsLead: Filing postmortem template now and CCing execs. ETA for RCA draft: EOD tomorrow.
Rachel: I'll start the RCA timeline and attach diffs.
Alicia: Closing handoff — oncall relieved at 07:20 UTC. Good job. :thumbsup:
Sam: logging final note: `rollback_not_required=true; pinned_to_v2.0=true; next_action=create_guardrails`
Jonah: +1.
Marco: +1."
